newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast to sell off part of state cotton firm.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast to sell off part of state cotton firm.

text.p: Ivory Coast has announced plans to sell-off part of the state cotton firm, Compagnie Ivoirienne pour le Developpement des Textiles (CIDT), one of West Africa's largest agro-industrial companies.

A cabinet statement, published on Friday in the government daily Fraternite Matin, said that six of the company's 10 factories would be split into two lots under the plan and sold to the private sector.

The government, it added, would retain a stake of no more than 30 percent in the companies buying the lots but would also sell part of its stake in what remains of the CIDT to a mix of producers, staff and Ivorian nationals.
The government said that the sell-off formed part of the liberalisation of the West African nation's cotton sector.

Ivory Coast set up the company in 1974 with France's Compagnie Francaise de Developpement des Textiles (CFDT). CFDT holds a 30 percent stake in the CIDT and will retain the same stake in the residue of the company.
CIDT lost money in the early 1990s but the 1994 devaluation of the CFA franc used in much of French-speaking Africa and a rise in world prices help push it back into profit in 1995.

CIDT has a monopoly on buying and marketing Ivory Coast's cotton crop. It is responsible for developing the cotton sector, for managing provision of inputs and providing credit to farmers, for research and for cotton ginning.
Under the plan, private ginning companies would be able to buy direct from producers within two years provided they assumed responsibility for supporting producers.
CIDT's 10 factories have a ginning capacity of 320,000 tonnes.
The two lots cover three factories in the north east, with combined processing capacity of 95,000 tonnes, and three in the north west, with a combined capacity of 115,000 tonnes.
The CIDT, which has capital of 7.2 billion CFA francs, retains control of the remainder.

The state will hold a 34 percent stake in the residue of the company, CFDT 30 percent. The rest will be sold to producers (20 pct), to staff (3 pct) and Ivorian nationals through the Abidjan Bourse (13 pct).
CIDT employs 1,640 people and controls the produce of 139,000 farmers, who, with their families, represent a population of 1.2 million people.
Ivory Coast has been busily privatising state companies as part of its economic liberalisation plans. It has sold stakes in 35 out of 58 earmarked for sale.
